title: Holistic SLO Pauser and Graceful Circuit Transitions for Regional Failover
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduce SLO pauser (temporary suspension of strict SLO enforcement) for coordinated regional failovers; add graceful circuit transition controller to ramp circuits and escrow retries to avoid retry storms; new metrics and alerts for pauser activity and graceful transitions.
description:
Motivation: During recent multi-region incidents we've seen aggressive SLO enforcement + immediate circuit flips trigger retry storms and cascading evictions. This PR introduces a small, guarded mechanism to temporarily relax enforcement during a coordinated failover window (SLO Pauser) and a controller that performs graceful circuit transitions (ramp-down/ramp-up and escrowed retries) to avoid oscillations.

Design summary: single continuous string: The change adds: 1) SLO Pauser: a planner that can be triggered by region health events or manual incident orchestration. When active it adjusts enforcement thresholds (softens eviction thresholds, extends grace windows) for a bounded time window and emits audit events so SRE/ops can monitor. 2) Graceful Circuit Transition Controller: replaces hard immediate circuit state flips with a staged transition (pre-drain, controlled-quarantine, soft-open). During transitions request retries are escrowed in a per-tenant short-lived queue with adaptive backoff, preventing a thundering herd while honoring priority tiers. 3) Metrics/tracing: new metrics pauser.active_seconds, pauser.trigger_cause, transition.state, transition.escalations_avoided plus tracing spans to correlate when pauser & transitions are used together. 4) Safety: Pauser requires dual-signal (either region-health AND at-least-one-slo-breached) OR explicit operator override. Time-bounded by default (5-15 minutes configurable) with automatic cooldown to prevent repeated toggles.

What changed (high level): Added a small orchestration component in src/runtime/control/pauser, introduced transition state machine in src/runtime/circuit, wiring into the existing scheduling and eviction paths, and added tests and monitoring. No changes to customer API surface.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc updated (Linear ENG-7654) - [x] Unit tests for state machine - [x] Integration test with simulated regional health events - [x] E2E canary in perf-lab (small cohort) - [x] Observability dashboards + alerts - [x] Safety kill-switch and operator docs

Testing and validation: Ran unit tests and integration harness across perf-lab (see commits). We saw a 4x reduction in peak retry attempts in the failover sim and no measurable regression in steady-state p50/p95 latency. Canary ran for 6h in staging with two staged failover drills.

Rollout plan: Feature is gated behind a runtime flag defaulting to off for existing clusters. We will enable for a small subset of regions (canary) for 48h, then 25% traffic, then global if stable. Ops playbook added in /docs/operational/playbooks/pauser.md.

Related work: complements regional-prefetch and staged-fallback changes (ENG-7810). This is intentionally conservative—pauser only relaxes enforcement thresholds, never disables core safety checks.

Notes: this intentionally avoids complicated tenant-specific heuristics in this iteration; follow-up will consider tenant budgets/credits for pauser use.

review_comments: Tom Nguyen: This looks promising. Can you clarify how pauser expiry interacts with automatic node drains? If a node drains while pauser is active do we honor node-level eviction?

Aisha Patel: Pauser does not block critical node-level drains; node drains still complete. Pauser only relaxes tenant-mapped SLO eviction thresholds and tenant-level immediate preemptions. Added a unit test to validate node drains are unaffected.
Sofia Ramirez: We should ensure we don't mask degraded-cpu situations by lowering thresholds. Suggest adding a CPU-based hard-fail path.
Aisha Patel: Agreed. Implemented: pauser has a hard-fail bypass if infra-level metrics (cpu/mem) exceed emergency thresholds; see pauser.go line 174.
Marcel König: CI flakes on integration test first run (timing-dependent). Consider increasing timeouts in the harness.
Aisha Patel: Increased timeouts + added deterministic clocks to test harness; re-ran CI.
Ops (approval): Verified the playbook and canary config. Good to go for canary rollout.
Tom Nguyen: Approved after addressing infra-level bypass and test determinism.

notes_for_oncall: If pauser triggers unexpectedly: 1) Check pauser.active_seconds and trigger_cause metrics in the Pauser dashboard. 2) Use runtime flag runtime.features.slo_pauser=false to immediately disable. 3) If rollback needed, merge revert PR that flips canary flags and redeploy.
